symptoms.label: Headache / Migraine
symptoms.reason: Neurologists specialize in diagnosing recurrent headaches, migraines, nerve-related cranial pain, and intracranial concerns.
symptoms.advice: Note the trigger factors, frequency, and whether light or sound sensitivity is present.

symptoms.label: Dizziness / Vertigo
symptoms.reason: Vertigo and balance issues commonly stem from inner ear vestibular disturbances, or neurological equilibrium issues.
symptoms.advice: Keep track of whether turning your head triggers spinning sensations.

symptoms.label: Eye Pain / Vision Issue
symptoms.reason: Ophthalmologists handle ocular inflammation, acute eye pain, visual disturbances, and cornea/retina examinations.
symptoms.advice: Avoid rubbing your eyes; seek emergency care immediately if sudden vision loss occurs.

symptoms.label: Ear Pain / Hearing Difficulty
symptoms.reason: ENT specialists treat middle and inner ear infections, eustachian tube blockages, and hearing disturbances.
symptoms.advice: Avoid inserting cotton buds or foreign objects into the ear canal.

symptoms.label: Sore Throat / Difficulty Swallowing
symptoms.reason: Pharyngeal inflammation, tonsillitis, and vocal cord irritation are evaluated by ENT or General Physicians.
symptoms.advice: Stay hydrated and monitor if accompanied by high fever or swollen glands.

symptoms.label: Neck Pain / Stiffness
symptoms.reason: Cervical spine strain, disc compression, and musculoskeletal stiffness are managed by Orthopedic specialists.
symptoms.advice: Avoid sudden neck jerks; maintain ergonomic posture while reading or working.

symptoms.label: Chest Pain / Heavy Pressure
symptoms.reason: Chest pressure or pain warrants immediate cardiac evaluation to assess coronary artery circulation and heart function.
symptoms.advice: If the pain radiates to the jaw, left arm, or causes cold sweats/breathlessness, call emergency services immediately.

symptoms.label: Burning Sensation / Acid Reflux
symptoms.reason: Substernal burning after meals is typically gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) or esophageal irritation.
symptoms.advice: Avoid lying down flat immediately after eating and note trigger foods.

symptoms.label: Palpitations / Rapid Heartbeat
symptoms.reason: Irregular rhythm, fluttering sensations, or tachyarrhythmias are investigated by Cardiologists.
symptoms.advice: Monitor if episodes occur at rest or during exertion, and limit caffeine.

symptoms.label: Shortness of Breath / Wheezing
symptoms.reason: Pulmonologists specialize in airways, asthma, bronchitis, and lung parenchymal disorders.
symptoms.advice: Seek immediate medical care if breathing becomes rapidly labored or lips turn pale/blue.

symptoms.label: Persistent Cough
symptoms.reason: Coughs extending past 2-3 weeks require respiratory evaluation, chest radiography, and airway assessment.
symptoms.advice: Note if the cough produces colored phlegm or occurs mainly during night.

symptoms.label: Stomach Pain / Cramping
symptoms.reason: Gastroenterologists diagnose gastritis, peptic ulcers, gall bladder issues, and digestive tract disorders.
symptoms.advice: Note whether the pain happens before meals, after eating, or wakes you at night.

symptoms.label: Nausea / Vomiting
symptoms.reason: Frequent nausea and gastrointestinal intolerance should be evaluated for viral gastritis or metabolic causes.
symptoms.advice: Sip electrolyte fluids frequently in small amounts to prevent dehydration.

symptoms.label: Bloating / Indigestion
symptoms.reason: Digestive enzyme deficiencies, gut dysmotility, or irritable bowel patterns are treated by gastroenterologists.
symptoms.advice: Keep a 3-day food log to pinpoint specific digestive sensitivities.

symptoms.label: Lower Abdominal Pain
symptoms.reason: Lower quadrant discomfort may indicate bowel irritation, diverticulitis, or acute appendiceal inflammation.
symptoms.advice: Consult immediately if pain localizes sharply to the lower right side with fever.

symptoms.label: Painful / Frequent Urination
symptoms.reason: Urologists specialize in the urinary tract, bladder infections, urethral inflammation, and kidney stones.
symptoms.advice: Increase fluid intake and avoid holding urine for prolonged periods.

symptoms.label: Pelvic Pain / Cramps
symptoms.reason: Pelvic region issues require targeted evaluation of reproductive organs or lower urinary tract pathways.
symptoms.advice: Document the correlation with menstrual cycles or physical movement.

symptoms.label: Shoulder / Elbow Joint Pain
symptoms.reason: Orthopedic doctors assess rotator cuff tears, tendonitis, arthritis, and joint dislocations.
symptoms.advice: Avoid heavy overhead lifting until clinically evaluated.

symptoms.label: Numbness / Tingling in Hand
symptoms.reason: Tingling or pins-and-needles down the arm points to cervical nerve root compression or carpal tunnel syndrome.
symptoms.advice: Note if symptoms worsen when typing or resting your wrist on hard surfaces.

symptoms.label: Muscle Strain / Weakness
symptoms.reason: Musculoskeletal strain or acute trauma to the upper limb is best addressed by Orthopedic specialists.
symptoms.advice: Apply cold compression for acute sprains within the first 48 hours.

symptoms.advice: Avoid heavy overhead lifting until clinically evaluated.

symptoms.label: Numbness / Tingling in Hand
symptoms.reason: Numbness or pins-and-needles down the arm points to peripheral neuropathy or nerve entrapment.
symptoms.advice: Note if symptoms worsen when typing or working on screens.

symptoms.label: Muscle Strain / Weakness
symptoms.reason: Musculoskeletal strain or acute trauma to the arm is best addressed by Orthopedic specialists.
symptoms.advice: Apply cold compression for acute sprains within the first 48 hours.

symptoms.label: Knee Pain / Swelling
symptoms.reason: Orthopedists diagnose ligament tears (ACL/meniscus), osteoarthritis, patellar tendonitis, and joint effusion.
symptoms.advice: Avoid high-impact jumping or squatting until the joint is evaluated.

symptoms.label: Ankle / Foot Pain
symptoms.reason: Sprains, plantar fasciitis, and stress fractures are managed by Orthopedic and Podiatric specialists.
symptoms.advice: Rest the foot elevated and wear supportive, cushioned footwear.

symptoms.label: Difficulty Walking / Weakness
symptoms.reason: Gait disturbances can be caused by joint degeneration or lumbar nerve root impingement (sciatica).
symptoms.advice: Use support while walking if balance feels compromised.

symptoms.label: Rash / Redness / Itching
symptoms.reason: Dermatologists manage eczema, contact dermatitis, fungal/bacterial skin infections, and allergic eruptions.
symptoms.advice: Avoid scratching and refrain from applying harsh fragranced lotions.

symptoms.label: Acne / Skin Blemish / Lesion
symptoms.reason: Dermatologists specialize in follicular inflammation, cystic acne, and abnormal mole/pigment changes.
symptoms.advice: Keep the area gently cleansed; do not pop or pinch blemishes.

symptoms.label: Lower Back Pain
symptoms.reason: Orthopedic spine specialists evaluate lumbar muscle strain, herniated discs, and facet joint arthritis.
symptoms.advice: Avoid heavy lifting or bending from the waist; maintain a neutral spine.

symptoms.label: Upper Back / Shoulder Blade Pain
symptoms.reason: Thoracic paraspinal tension, postural strain, or rib cage mechanics are treated by Orthopedics.
symptoms.advice: Perform gentle chest openers and check desk ergonomics.

emergency.reason: One or more of your reported symptoms are red flags that require immediate emergency evaluation to rule out life-threatening conditions such as subarachnoid haemorrhage, meningitis, or stroke.
emergency.advice: Please call emergency services (108 / 999 / 911) or go to the nearest Emergency Room immediately. Do not drive yourself.
emergency.emergencyNotice: 🚨 CRITICAL ALERT: Do not wait. Seek emergency care NOW.

outcome_primary_care_migraine.reason: Your headache features are consistent with a migraine pattern. A first or occasional migraine episode is best managed initially by a General Physician, who can confirm the diagnosis and initiate standard treatment.
outcome_primary_care_migraine.advice: Keep a headache diary (triggers, frequency, duration). Avoid known triggers such as skipped meals, poor sleep, or caffeine changes. Your doctor may prescribe triptans if appropriate.

outcome_neurology_migraine.reason: You are experiencing frequent migraines (more than 4 days/month). Neurologists specialise in migraine prophylaxis, acute rescue therapy, and identifying any structural causes for recurrent episodes.
outcome_neurology_migraine.advice: Request a neurology referral from your GP. Preventive medications (beta-blockers, topiramate, CGRP antagonists) or specialised procedures may be appropriate.

outcome_neurology_chronic.reason: Daily or near-daily headaches may indicate Chronic Daily Headache (CDH) or Medication Overuse Headache (MOH), requiring specialist neurological evaluation.
outcome_neurology_chronic.advice: Track all medications taken for headache relief — overuse of painkillers can worsen chronic headache. A neurologist will guide a supervised detox and preventive regimen.

outcome_general_medicine.reason: Your headache is responding to rest and basic pain relief, and no concerning features are present. This is likely a tension-type or stress-related headache best managed at primary care level.
outcome_general_medicine.advice: Stay hydrated, maintain regular sleep, and consider stress-reduction techniques. See a GP if headaches become more frequent or resistant to simple relief.

outcome_neurology_refractory.reason: A headache that is persistent and refractory to standard pain relief warrants specialist evaluation to rule out secondary causes such as raised intracranial pressure, cervicogenic headache, or structural abnormalities.
outcome_neurology_refractory.advice: Avoid exceeding the recommended dose of any pain medication. A neurologist may order imaging (MRI/CT) or refer to a headache clinic.
